name: Wizard of Oz Prototype
phase: Low-Fidelity Prototyping and Smoke Testing Tactics
hypothesis: We believe customers will trust an automated interface to handle [complex task]. We will verify this by building a functioning frontend facade operated entirely by humans on the back end, and consider it validated if users process ≥ 50 transactions with an average Net Promoter Score (NPS) ≥ 50 and an error rate below 5%.
schematic: Delivery at step 2 of the 3-step strip

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Build a polished front end wired to internal dashboards or spreadsheets instead of an automated backend.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Have people process each request in real time and answer through the interface.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Log turnaround time, interaction patterns, failures and completion.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Build a polished web frontend that mirrors a finished, automated product. Connect form inputs and workflows to internal operational dashboards, alerts, or spreadsheets rather than automated backends.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Deliver the experience in real time using human operators who process incoming requests, pull data manually, and send responses back through the system interface.

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Log end-to-end turnaround times, user interaction patterns, system failures, and post-task completion metrics.

warning.label: Unsustainable Fulfillment Expectations
warning.text: Operators smooth over bad data, faking product-market fit that breaks under automation.

warningFull: Human operators can often resolve confusing edge cases, fix typos, and smooth over bad data in ways that automated code cannot, creating a false impression of product-market fit that breaks down during actual software automation.
